note: Every case in tests/host_launch_diagnostics.rs is an execution of instrumented production code through an existing public seam of the eliot_host library target (HostLaunchOptions::{parse,parse_system_service,validate_service_main_argv}, classify_host_scm_inspection, validate_host_scm_bootstrap driven to its pre-SCM refusal). The facade is never called directly from the test target, so no expected log record is hand-constructed and no case compares the facade to itself. Records are read back out of a scoped tracing subscriber after real production code ran. Boundaries whose owner is a private module behind pub(super) items (host_job_launch, launch_artifact_lease, launch_descriptor_validation, store_kernel_launch_sequence, kernel_activation_driver, kernel_front_door_client) are proven by inline #[cfg(test)] cases in their owning file; the integration case names the owner and asserts the private source binding. Audit 5910159678: the two false readiness phase tokens are retired (see renamed_phase_tokens) and the frozen structured correlation now carries the owner-held identities. Sink outcome never alters result/order/status/cleanup. Package fixtures never claim live launch. Real Windows Event Log delivery smoke needs #984 and stays an honest residual: the seam is typed-Unavailable, never FFI, never faked.

single_terminal_ruling.host_start_failed_owner: lib.rs HostTerminalGuard (BOUNDARY_START_TERMINAL), the single terminal for one failed physical launch
single_terminal_ruling.scm_bootstrap_unknown_owner: scm_launch.rs ScmLaunchTerminalGuard, the single terminal for one failed SCM bootstrap validation, a different operation from a physical launch
single_terminal_ruling.note: The former host-launch-failed code is gone: HostLaunchTerminalGuard in host_job_launch.rs became phase-only so one failed launch emits exactly one host.terminal_error record. Exactly one of the eight instrumented files may still call observe_terminal_error.

correlation_contract: Every phase detail is rendered by LaunchPhaseCorrelation::render(phase) as single-space separated key=value pairs in correlation_keys order, phase first. Each &str value is bounded by host_diagnostics::bound_field; an identity the call site does not hold renders as the shared 'missing' value, so the emitted text carries exactly the markers listed in correlation_missing_markers ('<slot>=missing'), and is never invented, guessed from a constant, or left empty. The vocabulary has no pid slot: a reusable process id can never be recorded as a process-start identity.

renamed_phase_tokens.readiness_owner: src/kernel_activation_driver.rs DurableKernelActivationDriver::active is the only path allowed to emit a readiness claim
renamed_phase_tokens.note: The Store barrier is the caller's StoreLivenessEvidence (exact Job membership plus a running process) and the Kernel record fires right after launch_kernel returned a child handle. Both are physical liveness, never semantic readiness.
